traits: Shallow, cone-shaped holes dug overnight, 1-3 inches deep
Armored, cat-sized (15-17 inches, 8-17 lbs), terrible eyesight
Long, tapering snout and large front claws for digging
Digs where soil is soft and grubs or earthworms are plentiful

look_alikes.difference: Armadillo holes are small, cone-shaped, and scattered overnight; feral hog rooting tears up much larger patches of turf and soil in a single visit.
look_alikes.next_photo: A wide shot showing the size and shape of the disturbed area.

copy.what_it_means: It's digging your lawn because grubs and earthworms are there to eat — treating the food source usually sends the armadillo looking for better hunting elsewhere. Homeowners may legally live-trap nuisance animals per FWC rules.
copy.fact: When startled it jumps straight up — and it digs your lawn because grubs are there. Fix the grubs, lose the digger.
copy.blurb: We treat the grubs (the food source); the armadillo moves to better hunting on its own.

tech_notes: Treat the underlying grub population; armadillo relocation/removal follows FWC nuisance-wildlife rules (euthanize, release on-site, or relocate within-county with landowner permission).
